chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'adab narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isbahani, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who said: Yahya ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Furat al-Qazzaz informed me, saying: Harun ibn Ubaydat narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both).

Umar said when death approached him: 'I repent to God for three things: My usurping of this authority, myself and Abu Bakr, from the people; and my appointing myself as ruler over them; and my preferring some Muslims over others.'
ai.seo_question: What three things did Umar ibn al-Khattab repent for regarding his rule?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records Umar’s deathbed confession, highlighting the Shia critique of the early caliphate's legitimacy through the lens of 'ghasb' (usurpation) rather than mere election. This narration underscores the theological tension between the divine appointment of the Ahl al-Bayt and the pragmatic, yet contested, consolidation of power by the first two caliphs. It serves as a key textual evidence for Shia scholars arguing that the initial transfer of authority lacked the requisite divine mandate.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-225 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn al-Hassan al-Mo’adab quoted Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isbahany, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Saqafy, on the authority of Yahya ibn al-Hassan ibn al-Forat al-Qaz’zaz, on the authority of Harun ibn Ubaydat, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hassan ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB), “When Umar was facing death, he said, ‘I repent to God for the following three actions:1- Abu Bakr and I took the rule over the people from others;2- I forced the Caliph on the people;3- I ranked some people over others.’”
